extract features from intermediate layers

Source: R/im_features.R
extract_features.Rd

extract features from intermediate layers

Usage

extract_features(
  impath,
  layers,
  model = NULL,
  target_size = c(224, 224),
  spatial_pooling = "none"
)

im_features(
  impath,
  layers,
  model = NULL,
  target_size = c(224, 224),
  spatial_pooling = "none"
)

Arguments

impath

path to image file

layers

the layer indices

model

the Keras model

target_size

the target image dimensions (height, width) appropriate for the model

spatial_pooling

How to reduce 4-D feature maps (1 x H x W x C, as produced by convolutional layers) over height and width. One of:

"none"

(Default) No pooling. The full map is returned as a 4-D array.

"avg"

Global average pooling: the mean over all positions, giving a vector of length C.

"max"

Global max pooling: the maximum over all positions, giving a vector of length C.

"resize_HxW"

Resize the map to H by W and flatten, for example "resize_3x3" or "resize_7x7". Any positive H and W are accepted. This keeps coarse spatial layout and gives a vector of length H * W * C.

See the Spatial pooling section for details.

Value

A tibble with columns image, layer and a list-column feature. The tibble inherits class imfeatures_feature_tbl for dplyr compatibility.

Spatial pooling

Pooling trades spatial detail for size. For VGG-16 block5_conv3 (a 14 x 14 map with 512 channels), "none" keeps 100,352 values, "resize_3x3" keeps 4,608, and "avg" or "max" keep 512.

"resize_HxW" shrinks a map by area averaging: each output cell is the mean of the input positions it covers, with partial overlap weighted by area. Averaging the cells of a resized map therefore reproduces "avg". If the requested size is larger than the map in either direction, bilinear interpolation is used instead. Resizing runs in TensorFlow. If TensorFlow is unavailable, a warning is raised and the unpooled map is returned.

A resized or unpooled map is flattened with height varying fastest, then width, then channel. To recover the array from a flattened "resize_HxW" vector v, use array(v, dim = c(H, W, C)).

spatial_pooling only affects 4-D outputs. Dense layers such as fc1 have no spatial axes and are returned as they are.

These string options serve extract_features(), compute_feature_similarity() and extract_vgg_features(). For per-stage pooling, and for grid, DCT and radial pooling, use extract_feature_hierarchy with the pooler objects described in poolers.

See also

vignette("spatial-pooling", package = "imfeatures") for a comparison of all pooling options.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
# Extract features from a single image using default VGG16 model
img_path <- system.file("extdata", "example.jpg", package = "imfeatures")

# Extract features from multiple layers
features <- extract_features(
  impath = img_path,
  layers = c(3, 5, 7), # conv1_2, conv2_1, conv2_2
  model = NULL, # Uses default VGG16
  target_size = c(224, 224)
)

# Extract features with spatial pooling
features_pooled <- extract_features(
  impath = img_path,
  layers = c(10, 12), # Later convolutional layers
  spatial_pooling = "avg" # Global average pooling
)

# Extract features with spatial resizing
features_resized <- extract_features(
  impath = img_path,
  layers = c(10),
  spatial_pooling = "resize_7x7" # Resize spatial dimensions to 7x7
)

# Access the extracted features
layer3_features <- features$feature[[1]] # Features from layer 3
dim(layer3_features) # Check dimensions
} # }
